RFdiffusion3 is now a Science paper—and someone just showed how to poison the corpora that train protein designers.

BioTender Daily Papers #81: 6 new papers (arXiv 5 + Science 1) across 3 directions.

🧬 All-atom protein design & data-supply-chain security
• RFdiffusion3: puts backbone, side chains, and non-protein atoms (ligands, nucleic acids) in one all-atom diffusion frame so designs can take fine constraints (active sites, H-bonds, geometry, symmetry) up front. Reports better compute-benchmark design at lower inference cost, with experimental characterization of DNA-binding proteins and cysteine hydrolases — now peer-reviewed Science; wet success rates still vary by task and need case-by-case screens
• Poisoning protein-design corpora: attacks that contaminate autoregressive PLM pretraining data or only insert records into a text-guided generator’s retrieval store—no inference-code change needed—can make trigger words elicit preset sequences/domains. Stable triggers reported on ProtGPT2, ProGen2 variants, and retrieval-augmented systems while normal inputs look fine — arXiv preprint; needs reproduction on real large models and production DBs, but elevates provenance, signing, and corpus audit as design-safety problems

🧬 Panoramic single-cell modeling & EEG–text semantic alignment
• CellNet: encodes DNA-derived gene identity + measured RNA into a shared image-like representation to ease the high-frequency / limited-gene coverage of sc foundation models. Pretrained on 40 species, 231M cell profiles; evaluated on rare populations, condition-linked states, and missing-expression prediction, including masked coding genes and some noncoding targets, plus spatial and cross-species lineage patterns — arXiv preprint; watch database overlap, species skew, external zero-shot checks, and dedup
• EEG–text contrastive alignment for imagined speech: aligns EEG with a frozen text encoder’s semantic space (not 39 independent labels); EEG encoder learns EEG–sentence matching + text-prototype classification, with max cosine similarity as an internal reliability score. Fixed-class decoding ~dedicated classifiers, plus similarity retrieval / semantic-axis analysis on unseen candidate sentences — arXiv preprint; n=5 subjects; EMG, timing, and individual differences limit claims for open-vocab BCI

🌳 Long-horizon bioinformatics agents & clinical text extraction
• OmicsBench: research-scale multi-turn agent eval — 97 tasks → 662 interdependent subtasks in DAG order, deterministic answer keys, optional post-error context to test recovery. Across 12 models × 3 frameworks, best setups still far from saturated; steps that depend on prior results fail more; common failures include silently swapping statistical filters and hallucinating whole answers from memory — arXiv preprint; long-horizon, dependency-aware design exposes reproducibility gaps better than one-shot Q&A
• Dual-LLM consensus pipeline for Trofinetide phenotypes in Rett syndrome: from 108 patients on continuous trofinetide and 26,763 clinical notes, extracts 18 treatment-related phenotype classes via keyword screen → two-model agreement → patient–timepoint matrix. Architecture/prompts chosen only on a diarrhea development set, then frozen and transferred; expert spot-checks reported high agreement — arXiv preprint; measures whether a visit note records a phenotype, not clinical improvement; single-center, small labeled set, documentation bias

The common thread:
Capability is racing ahead of trust infrastructure. Peer-reviewed all-atom design sits next to corpus poisoning; panoramic sc models and EEG semantics next to agent evals that still break on long DAGs; clinical LLM pipelines that agree on documentation, not outcomes.

From Science-grade all-atom design → poisoned corpora → panoramic cells + imagined-speech EEG → long-horizon omics agents + dual-LLM clinical phenotyping.

AI VIDEO CREATORS, HAVE YOU EVER CONSIDERED SELLING SHORT ADVERTISING JINGLES TO BUSINESSES? 😭🔥

Not every advertisement needs a long voiceover.

Sometimes, a short, memorable musical message can make a brand's content more interesting.

And when you combine AI music tools with AI video creation, you can explore an entirely different service.

Let me show you how.

Imagine a restaurant launching a new meal combo.

Instead of creating an ordinary product advertisement, you develop a catchy 15-second musical commercial.

The food is beautifully presented.

There's a fun, original jingle.

The restaurant's name is clearly communicated.

And the video ends with the actual offer and ordering information.

Now imagine doing something similar for:

- Fashion brands
- Restaurants
- Schools
- Retail stores
- E-commerce businesses
- Event organizers

Here's how to start.

STEP 1: Learn how advertising jingles are structured.

A good jingle should communicate a brand's message, not just sound entertaining.

STEP 2: Practice writing short, original advertising lyrics.

STEP 3: Use appropriately licensed music and audio tools to develop your sound.

STEP 4: Combine the music with a well-directed AI video advertisement.

STEP 5: Build three demonstration commercials for fictional brands.

Then research businesses that might be interested in this style of advertising.

You can offer:

A 15-second musical advertisement.

A 30-second brand commercial.

Or a collection of short promotional jingles.

Check the commercial rights for every music and voice-generation tool you use. Don't imitate famous artists or copy recognizable songs without permission.

Here's the opportunity:

YOU CAN COMBINE STORYTELLING, MUSIC, VIDEO PRODUCTION, AND ADVERTISING INTO ONE CREATIVE SERVICE.

The more clearly you define what you're offering, the easier it becomes for a potential client to understand its value.

Continue my Beyond-RL series, now on the unsupervised training for diffusion models! 

Part II: https://t.co/mMqUFiTuQ8

I will go over three perspectives about diffusion models and how they lead to different unsupervised training algorithm design.

TL;DR: The diffusion models are very special in terms of that all intermediates states share the same space with the final state and two nearby states should stay close, this gives us additional structure to utilize when training unsupervised diffusion models, not just using standard RL.

1/  This one is somewhat older paper (DL lifecycle wise) but I think this is an important regularization idea to combat reward hacking! I’ve personally done this (before even reading this paper) and it’s stabilizes the loss landscape. 

DDRL: keep training on data while doing RL. They combine reward maximization with the usual diffusion loss on real/synthetic samples. That denoising loss helps keep generations realistic as the model learns to get higher rewards.
